title: Prompt Injection
content: Prompt injection is an attack where untrusted input embedded in a document or webpage tricks a language model into ignoring its original instructions and following the attacker's instructions instead. RAG applications are especially exposed because retrieved documents are fed directly into the model's context window.

title: RAG Poisoning
content: RAG poisoning happens when an attacker plants malicious or misleading content in a data source that a retrieval-augmented generation system indexes, so that later queries retrieve and surface the poisoned content as if it were trustworthy.

title: Vector Embeddings
content: A vector embedding is a numeric representation of text produced by an embedding model, positioned so that semantically similar text ends up close together in vector space. RAG systems compare a query's embedding against stored document embeddings to find relevant context.

title: Chunking
content: Chunking splits long documents into smaller overlapping pieces before embedding them, because embedding models and vector similarity search work best on focused passages rather than entire documents.

title: Least Privilege for Agents
content: The principle of least privilege says an AI agent should only be granted the minimum permissions and tool access needed to complete its task, which limits the damage a prompt injection or a compromised tool can cause.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
content: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is a technique that improves a language model's answers by first retrieving relevant passages from an external knowledge source, such as a vector database of embedded documents, and then adding those passages to the model's prompt as context. This lets the model answer questions about private or up-to-date information it was never trained on and reduces hallucination, though it also means the model trusts whatever the retriever returns.
